statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ futures have not quoted since Friday's 21:00 UTC close and Globex does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail stays low at 14%, the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. No pathological one-way price path can form while no venue is quoting, and the last observed path was benign.

What changed this hour is the geopolitical input, and it changed in both directions. Israeli strikes on south Lebanon on Saturday killed 11 people in villages including Deir al-Zahrani, the deadliest day since the June ceasefire, after a Hezbollah drone attack wounded three IDF soldiers. The IDF has since identified a second senior Hezbollah commander killed in those strikes, Defence Minister Katz has vowed to settle scores on all fronts, and Hezbollah's chief has called the ceasefire deal humiliating. Separately an IDF tank was hit by an explosive device in Gaza in what the military called a grave truce violation. That is a genuine, new, unresolved escalation arriving into a closed tape, and it is why Stress moves up to 80%.

Pulling the other way is the single most important macro overhang. Axios reports that IRGC leadership told the White House through a secret backchannel, via Kurdish intermediary Nechirvan Barzani, that it backs Tehran's negotiators - addressing the specific US concern that hardliners would obstruct any Hormuz agreement. The strait has been effectively shut since late February, with only 8 to 15 vessels crossing daily on 4-6 August against roughly 130 before the war, and Iran still demands sanctions relief and war reparations before reopening. A signal that the negotiating track is internally supported is the most constructive datum available on that file.

Stress is therefore raised but Tail is not, which is the correct asymmetry when signals conflict. Two observed facts hold the equity-path read down. VIX closed Friday at its lowest level of 2026, near 14.5. And the Russell 2000 set a record on Friday while the Nasdaq fell 0.28%, which is breadth broadening rather than the narrow leadership that typically precedes a one-way index break. Low implied volatility is thin cushion rather than evidence of safety, and that is a Stress statement, not a Tail one.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 14% maps to EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item this hour is scheduling rather than sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart is the only checkpoint inside this forecast window and the danger window is anchored to it at 21:55-00:00 UTC, 23:55-02:00 Berlin. That window is deliberately narrower than a whole-session shutdown: the risk is concentrated in the gap itself and the first two hours of thin Asian-transition liquidity, where an unpriced weekend of Lebanon and Gaza headlines meets a market that closed at its lowest volatility of the year. Forecast Tail drifts 14% to 19% through the remaining halt, steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting - orange, block new base entries - before easing back through the watch band and returning to green at 05:00 UTC Monday.

This is general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and it is not a recommendation to place any trade.
headline: CME weekend halt holds with about ten hours to the Globex restart: Friday's NQ close of 30,141.75 was benign and VIX finished at its 2026 low, but Israel's deadliest south-Lebanon strikes since the June ceasefire and a fraying Gaza truce lift Stress to 80% while an IRGC backchannel signal supports the Hormuz talks - Tail stays low at 14%, EA_ON and green, Confidence 75%
body:
Observed reference levels, all from Friday 14 August's close because nothing has traded since. NQU26 settled at 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, opening at 30,210.75 against a 30,188.50 previous close and holding a 254-point range of 30,028.50 to 30,283.00. It finished mid-range, roughly 2.7% below the 52-week high of 30,975.50 and far above the 22,961.50 low. There is no persistent directional efficiency in that, no shallow-pullback extension, no repeated failed retracement and no close near an extreme - the four things the contract requires before Tail belongs above 25%.

Cash indices agreed. The Nasdaq Composite closed 26,729, down 0.28%; the S&P 500 7,785, down 0.17%; the Dow 53,732, down 0.20%. The Russell 2000 rose 0.51% to 3,068, a fresh record. On the week the S&P added 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.1% while the Dow fell 0.6%. VIX closed at its 2026 low near 14.5.

Rates and commodities. The 2-year yield finished at 4.17%, up 3.1bp on the day but down 3.2bp on the week; the 10-year at 4.695%, up 5.6bp on the day and 3.8bp on the week. That is a modest bear-steepening rather than a cross-asset stress impulse. WTI rose $1.15 to $82.40 and Brent $1.45 to $88.52, up roughly 33% and 34% year on year - the standing price of a closed Hormuz, with the IEA warning of deeper global deficits. Gold added $16.90 to $4,437.30.

Semiconductors were mixed rather than aligned, which matters because aligned semis are one of the amplifiers that can manufacture index-level one-way structure. Broadcom fell 5.9% and Intel 2% with Nvidia slightly lower, while AMD gained 6.5%, Micron 2.3% and SanDisk 7.4%; Applied Materials guided Q4 revenue to $10.25bn. Dispersion inside the complex is the opposite of the alignment that would justify raising Tail.

Friday's macro was genuinely soft and deserves to be carried forward. July retail sales fell 0.6%, the worst print since May 2025, and preliminary consumer sentiment came in at 51.0 against 54.5 expected. Equities took this benignly because it reduced the perceived odds of a September Fed hike, but a weakening consumer is a real seed for a growth scare and is part of why Stress sits high while Tail does not.

Calendar. The verified seven-day US list is front-loaded with housing and survey data, with FOMC Minutes on Wednesday 19 August at 18:00 UTC, jobless claims on Thursday and the S&P Global flash PMIs on Friday 21 August as the high-impact anchors. Industrial production and capacity utilisation are omitted because two sources disagree materially on the release time. Note that the Jackson Hole symposium falls on 27-29 August, outside this window, with Kevin Warsh due to deliver his first keynote as Fed chair on 28 August - the larger catalyst sits just beyond the seven-day horizon.

Evidence quality. Confidence rises to 75%. Current index and futures levels, the day and 52-week ranges, VIX, both yields, oil, breadth, sector detail, weekend geopolitics and the seven-day calendar were all read directly from primary pages this hour, and they are mutually consistent. The one real gap is that no live price path exists at all - but during a scheduled venue halt that absence is a certain, known fact rather than an unreliable reading, which is why it caps Confidence at the bottom of the high band rather than pushing it down.

lookbackSummary:
The trailing 24 hours run from 11:00 UTC Saturday to 10:00 UTC Sunday and sit entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours and the outcome was identical each time: EA_ON, green, dominantMode mixed. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 13%. Stress carried all of the movement, running 53, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then dipping to 70 and climbing 71, 71, 78, 79 and 78. Confidence rose steadily from 61% to 74%.

Two features of that track matter for reading the current hour. First, the Stress climb from 53 to the high seventies happened across a market that never quoted once - it is a re-reading of a static evidence set as the reopen approached, not a response to observed deterioration, and it should not be extrapolated mechanically. Second, the near-monotonic Confidence rise is genuine: successive hours added primary-source coverage of levels, volatility, rates, oil, breadth and the calendar even though the price path stayed unavailable.

Against that history the current hour is the first in the window with materially new information rather than a re-reading. The Saturday Lebanon strikes and the Gaza truce violation are new escalation, and the Axios report of an IRGC backchannel endorsement of Tehran's negotiators is a new de-escalation. Stress moves to 80% on the net, and Tail moves only one point to 14% because none of it is price-path evidence.
outlookSummary:
The next 24 hours end at 10:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart and the first twelve hours of live quoting sit inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for 10 of 24 slots, drifting 14% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting before easing through 24%, 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 05:00 UTC Monday, settling at 17% through the European morning. Forecast status is yellow at 21:00 UTC, orange at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow through 04:00 UTC Monday and green thereafter.

That orange is conditional risk about the reopen, not an assertion that a one-way path has been observed. The reasoning is mechanical: a full weekend of unpriced Lebanon, Gaza and Hormuz headlines has to clear into a single restart in thin liquidity, against a market whose implied volatility closed at the lowest level of 2026. If the gap is small and mean-reverting within the first hour, these forecast numbers will prove too high and the next assessments should say so.

Stress rises from 80% to a peak of 86% at the restart, then decays to 75% by 10:00 UTC Monday as the weekend stack is absorbed. Confidence dips to 72% through the last hours of the halt as the evidence ages, then rises sharply to 85% once live quoting restores the price path that is the single missing input. dominantMode is mixed throughout except for event/whipsaw across the four hours spanning the restart. Beyond this window the sequence is FOMC Minutes on Wednesday, jobless claims on Thursday and the flash PMIs on Friday, with Jackson Hole and Warsh's first keynote as chair on 27-29 August the larger catalyst just past the horizon.
